description: I'm Giuliano, a Brazilian Software Architect, CTO, and tech entrepreneur specializing in AI, software engineering, cloud computing, and mission-critical systems. I love turning complex challenges into practical solutions. At NASA Space Apps 2026, Ketlen and I are building StarSense, an AI-powered astronaut health monitoring platform. We combine engineering, innovation, product strategy, and UX to help make long-duration space missions safer.
summary:
StarSense: AI-Powered Contactless Health Monitoring for Space Exploration

StarSense is an innovative, non-invasive health monitoring system designed to support astronaut well-being during long-duration space missions.

Using Wi-Fi Sensing technology, ESP32 microcontrollers, and onboard artificial intelligence, StarSense analyzes variations in wireless signals to detect movement, breathing patterns, and behavioral changes without requiring body-worn sensors.

Unlike traditional wearable monitoring systems, StarSense aims to reduce physical discomfort, equipment dependency, and maintenance requirements while enabling continuous, contactless observation.

The system combines real-time signal processing, intelligent data analysis, and a centralized dashboard to identify potential health-related changes and support preventive decision-making.

Designed with scalability, energy efficiency, and accessibility in mind, StarSense explores a new approach to astronaut health monitoring, with potential applications in space habitats, remote environments, and healthcare on Earth.

StarSense transforms invisible wireless signals into actionable health intelligence, helping make space exploration safer and more sustainable.
details:
StarSense
Contactless AI-Powered Astronaut Health Monitoring


Project Overview

StarSense is an innovative, non-invasive health monitoring system designed to support astronaut safety and well-being during long-duration space missions.

Traditional astronaut health monitoring relies on specialized medical equipment, wearable sensors, and periodic physiological assessments. Although effective, these approaches can introduce challenges related to equipment dependency, physical comfort, energy consumption, and continuous monitoring.

StarSense explores a complementary approach: transforming existing wireless signals into meaningful indicators of human activity and physiological behavior.

By combining **Wi-Fi Sensing, ESP32 microcontrollers, signal processing, and artificial intelligence**, StarSense investigates how wireless signal variations can support continuous, contactless monitoring inside space habitats.

Our vision is to make preventive health monitoring more accessible, scalable, and less dependent on body-worn devices.

How StarSense Works

StarSense uses Wi-Fi Channel State Information (CSI) to analyze how wireless signals change as they propagate through an environment.

Human movement, posture changes, and respiratory motion can influence wireless signal characteristics. These variations provide a potential source of information about human activity without requiring physical contact.

The proposed system operates through five stages:

  1. Wireless Signal Acquisition: ESP32 microcontrollers capture Wi-Fi signal characteristics and variations.
  2. Signal Processing: The system processes measurements to identify temporal patterns associated with movement and other detectable physical activity.
  3. AI-Assisted Analysis: Analytical algorithms and artificial intelligence support the interpretation of signal patterns and the identification of potential behavioral changes.
  4. Health-Related Indicators: The platform explores indicators related to activity, movement, and breathing patterns.
  5. Monitoring Dashboard: A centralized interface visualizes measurements, historical trends, and potential alerts to support preventive observation

StarSense is designed as a complementary monitoring technology rather than a replacement for clinically validated medical instruments.

Key Features and BenefitsContactless Monitoring

The system explores physiological and behavioral observation without requiring astronauts to continuously wear dedicated sensing devices.


Continuous Observation

Wi-Fi Sensing offers the potential for repeated environmental measurements, supporting the identification of changes over time.

Low-Cost Hardware

ESP32 microcontrollers provide an accessible platform for experimentation, prototyping, and future optimization.

AI-Assisted Preventive Intelligence

By analyzing historical patterns, StarSense aims to identify meaningful deviations that could support further investigation by medical teams.

Modular Architecture

The platform is designed to accommodate additional sensing methods, environmental information, and future physiological monitoring capabilities.

Reduced Dependence on Wearables

Contactless sensing could complement conventional monitoring systems during periods when body-worn equipment is inconvenient or unavailable.

Technical Architecture

StarSense combines hardware, wireless sensing, software processing, and visualization.


Hardware:
  • ESP32 microcontrollers
  • BLE ELA Sensors and beacons
  • Wi-Fi communication infrastructure
  • Local computing resources for signal processing and data analysis

Core Technologies:

  • Wi-Fi Channel State Information (CSI)
  • Wireless signal acquisition and processing
  • Time-series analysis
  • Artificial intelligence and pattern recognition
  • Real-time data visualization

Data Processing Pipeline:

Wi-Fi Signals → ESP32 Acquisition → Signal Processing → Pattern Analysis → Health-Related Indicators → Monitoring Dashboard

The architecture prioritizes modularity, accessibility, and future integration with space habitat monitoring systems.

NASA Scientific Resources

NASA scientific resources were researched to support the project's conceptual and technical foundation.

These include:

  • NASA Open Science Data Repository (OSDR): Biological research and datasets related to the effects of spaceflight.
  • NASA Human Research Roadmap: Scientific information about astronaut health risks and long-duration missions.
  • NASA DONKI: Space weather events relevant to environmental risk awareness.
  • NASA RadLab: Radiation measurement research and environmental exposure information.

These resources help contextualize potential applications of StarSense in astronaut health monitoring and the broader space environment.

They are referenced as research resources, not as clinically validated training data or confirmed live API integrations.

Innovation and Creativity

StarSense introduces a different perspective on health monitoring: using wireless communication signals as an additional source of human activity information.

Its innovation lies in combining:

  • Contactless sensing using Wi-Fi signal variations.
  • Affordable and accessible ESP32 hardware.
  • Artificial intelligence for temporal pattern analysis.
  • Preventive monitoring concepts for space exploration.
  • A modular approach that can be expanded with additional environmental and physiological data.

Rather than requiring a dedicated sensor attached to every individual, StarSense investigates how sensing infrastructure within a habitat could provide complementary observations.

This approach has potential applications in spacecraft, orbital stations, future lunar habitats, remote research facilities, and terrestrial healthcare environments.

Challenges and Technical Limitations

Wi-Fi Sensing presents important technical challenges, including signal interference, environmental reflections, multipath propagation, individual movement differences, and the complexity of distinguishing multiple occupants.

Respiratory monitoring requires careful signal processing and validation against established reference measurements.

Wi-Fi CSI does not directly measure bone density, radiation exposure, or cardiac electrical activity. Any future assessment of these conditions would require additional sensors, validated datasets, or complementary medical technologies.

The use of ESP32 hardware in operational space missions would also require environmental, electromagnetic compatibility, reliability, and flight qualification assessments.

StarSense is therefore presented as a research prototype and a foundation for further experimental validation, not as a certified medical device or flight-qualified space system.

Expected Impact

StarSense aims to contribute to the development of accessible, intelligent, and non-invasive monitoring technologies for human space exploration.

Its potential benefits include:

  • Supporting long-term observation of astronaut activity.
  • Reducing dependence on wearable-only monitoring approaches.
  • Providing additional information for preventive health assessment.
  • Exploring low-power, low-cost sensing architectures.
  • Supporting future research into human behavior in confined environments.

Beyond space exploration, the underlying technology could eventually support monitoring applications in assisted living, remote healthcare, disaster response, and isolated environments.

Future Development

The proposed development roadmap includes:

  1. Improving Wi-Fi CSI acquisition and signal quality.
  2. Validating respiratory and movement estimates against reference devices.
  3. Developing individual identification and multi-person signal separation methods.
  4. Evaluating long-term behavioral and activity trends.
  5. Integrating relevant NASA scientific datasets and environmental information.
  6. Improving edge AI processing and predictive analysis.
  7. Testing performance in controlled environments that simulate selected space habitat conditions.
Conclusion

StarSense explores a future where wireless infrastructure does more than connect devices: it also contributes to understanding human activity and supporting preventive health monitoring.

By combining Wi-Fi Sensing, ESP32 microcontrollers, and artificial intelligence, the project investigates how invisible wireless signal variations can become useful health-related information.

StarSense: Turning Invisible Signals into Preventive Health Intelligence for the Future of Space Exploration.
